Apple TV: what the app cannot rebuild survives tvOS emptying its folders. Every folder a tvOS app may write is a cache that tvOS empties when the device runs low on storage and the app is closed; only the app's defaults are kept (500 KB by Apple's tvOS guide; tvOS ends an app whose defaults reach 1 MB). The settings, the profiles with their keys, the state, the install id, the split lists and CONNECT's sign-in session go through IAppFileStore (AppOptionsContext.FileStore): plain files everywhere but tvOS, where VpnHoodIosApp keeps them as entries of the defaults (UserDefaultsFileStore over KeyValueFileStore, a 256 KB budget: a change past it fails and the old value stays); the log, the caches and the downloads stay files. The proxies' database, which the extension opens, stays a file, so on tvOS a copy of the proxies the person added (ProxyEndPointCopy) refills it when it comes back empty; a URL's proxies come back with the URL. A real Apple TV lets an app write only a shared container's Library/Caches, though the simulator allows the root, where IosDevice made the VPN service's two folders: on tvOS they are under Library/Caches. Breaking: PortalAuthenticationProvider takes the store first (each CONNECT head passes context.FileStore), as do AppSettingsService and VpnProfileService; the unused VpnHoodApp.HasDebugCommand(storageFolderPath, command) and AppUtils.BuildFileSignature are gone, the split lists signing through the store. Docs: architecture-and-ipc.md's App Group folders, the privacy manifests' UserDefaults reason (CA92.1), CHANGELOG.Packages.md. Checked: tests for a TV's folders emptied between two runs, the budget and the proxies' copy, with the app library's suite and the split tests; CONNECT's heads build; on the tvOS 27 simulator, CLIENT's app with the terms accepted by the remote, its caches and the App Group's emptied, then launched again: the home, not the terms, and the same install id.

Apple TV: the Siri Remote's Menu goes back. Avalonia hands Menu (‹ on the newer remotes) to the app as the context-menu key (Key.Apps), not as Back, so MainView took no press of it and tvOS closed the app from every page, which App Review checks. On tvOS MainView takes Key.Apps as Back; on the first page GoBack leaves the press to the system, which shows the TV's Home screen, as tvOS asks. Checked on the tvOS 27 simulator with an XCUITest pressing the remote, before and after: Menu on Remote Access went to the TV's Home screen, and now goes back to the home with the focus on the row that opened the page; Menu on the home shows the TV's Home screen.
